rawFindings.title: Incorrect use of '_baseRoute' removed without adjusting its behavior in 'app.VERB' methods
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces usage of '_baseRoute' method inside the 'methods.forEach' loop for registering HTTP verb handlers with a direct call to 'this._router.route(path)'. The '_baseRoute' method implements caching of routes to prevent creating multiple route instances for the same path. Removing this caching can cause multiple route instances for the same path, breaking route handler overriding semantics and potentially causing unexpected behavior.
rawFindings.suggestion: Retain or replace the caching behavior of '_baseRoute' when replacing its usage. If the '_baseRoute' is removed, ensure 'this._router.route(path)' usage behaves equivalently with caching or provide alternative route caching strategy.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect method routing for HTTP verbs other than GET
rawFindings.explanation: The patched code removes the use of _baseRoute for routing and instead calls this._router.route(path) directly without calling lazyrouter beforehand in the method delegate inside methods.forEach. This breaks the guarantee that the router is initialized before use, and may cause routes to not be registered properly, especially for non-GET methods.
rawFindings.suggestion: Call this.lazyrouter() before accessing this._router.route(path) in the method delegate for all HTTP verbs to ensure the router is initialized and consistent.

rawFindings.title: Remove undefined _baseRoute usage which is deleted
rawFindings.explanation: The original code used an internal _baseRoute() function to get or create route objects, which managed caching routes for performance and case sensitivity. This function has been deleted in the patch, but the app.VERB and app.all methods no longer use it, directly calling this._router.route(). Removing _baseRoute may cause regression if caching or case insensitive behavior was relied upon.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore or re-implement _baseRoute method or ensure the new direct calls to this._router.route() preserve behavior such as caching and case normalization as was done before with _baseRoute.
